currentContext.business: Radiant Cash Management Services Limited operates an end-to-end portfolio spanning cash logistics, cash management and digital financial services, delivered through an integrated business portfolio of Retail Cash Management, Cash Processing, Network Currency Management, Cash Van Operations, Valuable Logistics and Fintech. It serves leading banks, NBFCs, retail and e-commerce customers and government institutions, with deep physical presence across urban, semi-urban and rural India supported by proprietary applications, API integrations and cloud infrastructure. Its cash logistics vehicles operate under RBI/MHA guidelines, and the group also runs a fintech subsidiary offering merchant ecosystem, Business Correspondent and digital banking access services.

risks.note: As a cash management service company the business involves sensitive financial data, and any disruption or leakage would endanger the company; timely and secure transmission of data is critical to operations. Mitigated through a cybersecurity policy and data storage and transmission facilities with 100% backups. Flagged with negative financial implications.

Poor labour management is identified as a significant risk that can lead to service disruptions and adverse impact on the Company's reputation, with workforce expectations rising over time. Mitigation is continuous interaction with the workforce and swift grievance redressal. Flagged with negative financial implications.

Stricter government regulation to mitigate climate change and reduce carbon emissions exposes the company to legal issues and penalties. The nature of vehicles used for cash logistics operations is regulated by RBI/MHA guidelines; vehicles in Delhi and NCR have been switched to CNG from petrol/diesel, with periodic pollution control checks and regular servicing. Flagged with negative financial implications.

risks.risk: Human rights compliance across the operating footprint
risks.note: Violation of human rights in any location where the company has business interest would result in agitations and loss of productivity. The company commits to prohibition of child labour, prohibition of forced and compulsory labour and freedom of association, with periodic human rights training and open field-team feedback channels. Flagged with negative financial implications.

risks.risk: Business ethics, anti-money-laundering and regulatory conduct
risks.note: Operating in the financial industry, adherence to anti-corruption, anti-money laundering, insider trading, fair taxation and auditing practices is key to operations; non-adherence would lead to legal fines. Identified as a material responsible-business-conduct issue.

Continued losses in the Valuable Logistics business, alongside higher operating expenses, held back profitability during the year even though revenue was broadly stable; the business remains in a consolidation phase with the payoff from prior-year efforts still pending.

risks.risk: Fintech subsidiary performance and policy dependence
risks.note: The decline in consolidated profitability was primarily attributable to the fintech subsidiary Aceware Fintech Services Private Limited, whose performance was impacted by the discontinuation of the RBI Payment Infrastructure Development Fund (PIDF) subsidy scheme and increased manpower — a direct dependence of subsidiary economics on a regulator-run subsidy scheme.

one-line thesis: Radiant delivered stable FY25 growth driven by Acemoney's 530% revenue surge and cost discipline, with margins improving despite muted core cash business; the key shift is the strategic pivot toward high-growth fintech and valuables logistics as new profit engines, reducing reliance on volatile BFSI cash flows.
financial scorecard: revenue: +10.6% YoY; EBITDA/margin: +12.5% YoY, 17.9% (improved 31 bps); PAT (rptd): +5.8% YoY; PAT (normalized): +15% YoY (ex-RVL losses); order book: not disclosed; net debt: INR80cr cash balance, net debt negative
guidance: revenue growth: mid- to high-teens CAGR (15-18%) over next 3 years; margin: aspiration to return to 20%+ EBITDA margins; order inflow: target 90,000 POS machines in FY26; capex/commissioning: incremental capex for RVL pan-India scaling post-lane validation
segment / subsidiary detail: Cash Van Operations: +40% revenue growth; Direct Clients: 15% of revenue (up from 5.2%); Acemoney: INR219cr revenue, 20%+ EBITDA margin, 64,228 POS installed; RVL: <1% revenue, breakeven targeted by Q1FY26; Insta Credit: launched FY25, market reception positive
growth verticals / optionality: Rural fintech penetration (50%+ merchant outlets still cash-only); jewelry logistics market (1.35L jewelers, only 25K serviced); direct B2B cash services to unbanked retail chains; cross-selling Insta Credit to Acemoney merchants
margins & cost dynamics: EBITDA margin improvement driven by cost control, Acemoney profitability, and RVL loss reduction; fixed cost leverage under pressure due to muted core revenue growth; RVL costs partially absorbed via shared van/guard infrastructure with RCMS
capex / expansion: Capex focused on Acemoney POS deployment (90K target FY26) and RVL specialized vehicles/software; no major capex beyond incremental scaling; existing cash logistics infrastructure leveraged for RVL
capital allocation: Prioritizing organic growth in Acemoney and RVL; cash balance of INR80cr provides flexibility for strategic acquisitions; no dividend or buyback mentioned; Acemoney acquisition model (high ROI) as template for future M&A
risks & watch-items: Sluggish BFSI demand (MFI/personal loan); UPI adoption in Tier 4/5; RVL breakeven delay; high fixed cost structure limiting margin expansion without revenue growth; regulatory scrutiny on fintech data security (mitigated by PCI DSS)
management quality / tone: Confident and strategic; focused on long-term secular trends (cash-in-circulation, rural digitization); transparent about RVL losses and timeline; optimistic on Acemoney scalability; committed to margin recovery
non-obvious takeaways: Acemoney's transaction-based revenue model (not device sales) creates sticky, scalable unit economics; RVL's 50-50 air/road split leverages existing cash logistics network without new capex; cash loss rates near zero due to ex-service culture, not just tech

themes.title: Digital platforms, SaaS, payments & cybersecurity
themes.need: Digital-public-infrastructure scale, enterprise SaaS and a compliance/security upcycle drive a distinct platform cohort. PINELABS/NPST/CMSINFO on payments; AURIONPRO/NEWGEN/NUCLEUS/ROUTE/TANLA on banking/CPaaS software; EMUDHRA/META(544441)/AURIONPRO on digital-identity & cybersecurity; CAPILLARY/MAPMYINDIA/NAZARA on SaaS/geospatial/gaming. Q1FY27 anchored the payments leg: PAYTM's GMV grew 31% YoY (accelerating 23% -> 27% -> 31%) with merchant payments about 80% of the financial-services mix and 25-30 lakh device additions a year on a distribution-only lending model (no book, no FLDG); MOBIKWIK posted payments GMV of INR 52,400cr (+58% YoY), a 13th consecutive record quarter and India's largest wallet by GTV at ~20% share, against only ~INR 3,200cr of digital-credit GMV. OFSS adds the banking-software annuity, with RPO +17% YoY versus revenue +7% and licence-and-cloud revenue +13% at a 44% operating margin.
themes.driver: Deal/ARR additions; festive digital-payments TPV; merchant-device additions; RBI/regulatory compliance-driven security spend.

themes.title: Logistics, ports & supply-chain formalization
themes.need: E-commerce, quick-commerce and GST-driven warehousing consolidation plus a 1P->3P shift drive an integrated-logistics up-cycle. DELHIVERY hit early FCF (>1B parcels, Express +46% rev) with Express targeting 16-18% margin; CONCOR/GATEWAY/JSWINFRA on rail/ports; ALLCARGO/MAHLOG/TVSSCS/VRLLOG on 3PL/road; BLUEDART/TCIEXP/WCIL/SNOWMAN on express + cold-chain; DELHIVERY/SHADOWFAX on quick-commerce fulfilment. Q1FY27's clearest turnaround datapoint: MAHLOG swung to a +INR 25.4cr PAT from a -INR 10.8cr loss on +23% revenue, with B2B Express (Rivigo) gross margin turning +6% from -3.8% and its EBITDA loss cut to -INR 1.6cr from -INR 11.8cr, guided to EBITDA breakeven within FY27, while Contract Logistics grew 26% with margin diluted only ~46bps on new-site start-up costs (opening a site almost every week).
themes.driver: Express/quick-commerce volume momentum; warehousing leasing; port/rail throughput; operating-leverage inflection.

one_liner.body: Radiant Cash Management Services is an integrated cash logistics, cash management and digital financial services provider with a nationwide network covering 14,844 PIN codes.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Radiant Cash Management Services Limited operates an end-to-end portfolio spanning cash logistics, cash management and digital financial services, delivered through an integrated business portfolio of Retail Cash Management, Cash Processing, Network Currency Management, Cash Van Operations, Valuable Logistics and Fintech. It serves leading banks, NBFCs, retail and e-commerce customers and government institutions, with deep physical presence across urban, semi-urban and rural India supported by proprietary applications, API integrations and cloud infrastructure. Its cash logistics vehicles operate under RBI/MHA guidelines, and the group also runs a fintech subsidiary offering merchant ecosystem, Business Correspondent and digital banking access services.

Does not participate in the Business Responsibility initiatives of the listed entity. Related-party arrangements run up to March 31, 2027 (board approval 23rd May, 2025) and cover commission for onboarding merchants and Business Correspondent (BC) agents, reimbursement of remuneration for personnel on deputation, inter-corporate loan and corporate guarantee.
- Acemoney Payment Solutions Private Limited — subsidiary: Named in Form AOC-1 as a subsidiary that was liquidated or ceased during the year.
- Radiant Protection Force Private Limited — related party: Related party under significant influence; material arm's-length contracts up to March 31, 2026 (board approval 18th February, 2023; shareholder approval by postal ballot dated March 23, 2023 covering FY 2023-24 to FY 2025-26) for services of gunmen, guards and drivers, lease rentals of vehicles, generators and cash vans, fleet operating and service charges, cash van running and maintenance expenses including reimbursement of expenses, lease rent for office premises, and an inter-corporate loan.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Hybrid payments economy: cash and digital transactions coexist, with currency in circulation at an all-time high of Rs 41.6 trillion in FY 2026 while UPI transaction value rose to Rs 314 trillion, creating sustained demand for secure cash logistics and digitally connected operations
- Financial inclusion: expanding banking access and merchant digitisation are creating greater demand for organised cash management and assisted banking services
- Economic formalisation: greater regulatory compliance, organised retail expansion and increasing digital adoption continue to support organised cash logistics providers
- Growing outsourcing: banks and enterprises are increasingly entrusting treasury, cash handling and secure logistics to specialised service providers
- Regional growth: rising economic activity in Tier II and Tier III markets continues to support demand for reliable last-mile cash logistics
- Technology-led operations: automation, real-time visibility and intelligent digital systems are enhancing efficiency, security and service quality across the cash management value chain
- Macro backdrop: India's real GDP expanded 7.7% in FY 2025-26 with inflation moderating to 3.48%, and GDP is projected to grow 6.6% in FY 2027 on sustained capital investment, improving credit offtake and resilient domestic consumption
- Near-term profitability drag: revenue was broadly stable but profitability was hit by higher operating expenses and continued losses in the Valuable Logistics business, which management says is in its consolidation phase with prior-year efforts expected to materialise in the current financial year
- Consolidated profitability decline attributed to the fintech subsidiary Aceware Fintech Services Private Limited, whose performance was impacted by the discontinuation of the RBI Payment Infrastructure Development Fund (PIDF) subsidy scheme and increased manpower

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: EBITDA margin improvement driven by cost control, Acemoney profitability, and RVL loss reduction; fixed cost leverage under pressure due to muted core revenue growth; RVL costs partially absorbed via shared van/guard infrastructure with RCMS

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Prioritizing organic growth in Acemoney and RVL; cash balance of INR80cr provides flexibility for strategic acquisitions; no dividend or buyback mentioned; Acemoney acquisition model (high ROI) as template for future M&A

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The annual report describes no physical plant or capacity expansion project. Radiant's expansion narrative for FY 2025-26 is asset-light and technology- and footprint-led: it migrated its ERP environment to AWS Cloud to strengthen scalability, business continuity and operational resilience, built out customer-facing technology through API integration with client ERP systems, the Client View Portal, the Radmus and Radiant Sandesh mobile applications, CPIN/OTP authentication and QR-enabled cash collection, and strengthened secure operations through CERT-In certified Vulnerability Assessment and Penetration Testing and modern software engineering tooling (SonarQube, Bitbucket Pipelines). Management states these investments position the company to support future growth with greater agility and provide scalable digital infrastructure. On the people side, the company expanded its workforce to 2,641 employees nationwide to support business expansion, operational requirements and evolving customer expectations, adding 8 leadership inductions and running 15+ training programmes. No commissioning dates, project names or capex quantum for any expansion project are disclosed in this bundle; the only rupee capital figure disclosed is the capital commitments note.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Nationwide physical network of 14,844 PIN codes, 9,162 operational locations and 77,521 customer touchpoints spanning urban, semi-urban and rural India
- Integrated solutions combining cash logistics, processing, cash management, fintech and valuable logistics in a single end-to-end portfolio
- Falling customer concentration: top 10 clients contributed 70% of revenue in FY 2026 versus 80% in FY 2024, and top 5 clients 49% versus 58%
- Technology enablement through AWS cloud migration of the ERP environment, API integration with client ERP systems and real-time transaction visibility
- Enduring customer relationships built on consistent execution and service excellence, with a marquee client base of leading banks, NBFCs, retail, e-commerce and government institutions
- Compliance-led operations backed by standardised SOPs, a risk management framework and a skilled workforce of 2,641 employees
- Regulated operating environment: vehicles used for cash logistics operations are governed by RBI/MHA guidelines, favouring organised providers
